'''Calibre''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|k|æ|l|ɪ|b|ər}} {{respell|KAL|ih|bər}})<ref>{{cite web |last=Salvette |first=Paul |date=21 August 2011 |title=Calibre Tutorial – eBook Formatting |url=http://www.paulsalvette.com/2011/08/calibre-tutorial-ebook-formatting.html |access-date=9 December 2025 |quote=Calibre (pronounced "[[Caliber]]") is an eBook library management system that is open source.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Goyal |first=Kovid |date=2009 |title=About Calibre: History |url=https://calibre-ebook.com/about#history |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251208223139/https://calibre-ebook.com/about#history |archive-date=2025-12-08 |access-date=2025-12-17 |website=calibre-ebook.com |quote=The name calibre was chosen by my wife, Krittika. The libre in calibre stands for freedom, indicating that calibre is a free and open source product, modifiable by all. Nonetheless, calibre should be pronounced as cali-ber, not ca-libre.}}</ref> is a [[cross-platform]] [[free and open-source]] [[Software suite|suite]] of [[e-book]] software. Calibre supports organizing existing e-books into virtual libraries, displaying, editing, creating and converting e-books, as well as syncing e-books with a variety of e-readers. Calibre has a large collection of community contributed plugins.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Index of calibre plugins |url=https://plugins.calibre-ebook.com/ |access-date=12 December 2023 |website=plugins.calibre-ebook.com}}</ref>

==History==
On 31 October 2006, when [[Sony]] introduced its [[Sony Reader|PRS-500]] [[e-reader]], Kovid Goyal started developing ''libprs500'', aiming mainly to enable use of the PRS-500 formats on [[Linux]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=9 October 2013 |title=Interview: Kovid Goyal, creator of calibre |url=https://en.softonic.com/articles/interview-kovid-goyal-creator-of-calibre |newspaper=Softonic}}</ref> With support from the MobileRead forums, Goyal [[reverse engineering|reverse-engineered]] the proprietary Broad Band eBook ([[BBeB]]) file format. In 2008, the program, for which a graphical user interface was developed, was renamed "calibre", displayed in all lowercase.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 2009 |title=calibre – About |url=https://calibre-ebook.com/about#history |access-date=29 July 2013 |website=Calibre-ebook.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Why the name calibre? |url=https://manual.calibre-ebook.com/faq.html#why-the-name-calibre |access-date=7 April 2025 |website=Calibre-ebook.com}}</ref>

In 2025, starting with version 8.11.1, Goyal began integrating [[large language model]]s into Calibre. Supported platforms include [[Google]], [[GitHub]], OpenRouter, Ollama, and LM Studio.<ref name="y543">{{cite web | last=Rudra | first=Sourav | title=AI Comes to Open Source eBook Reader Calibre | website=It's FOSS | date=2025-09-29 | url=https://itsfoss.com/news/ai-comes-to-calibre/ | access-date=2026-02-14}}</ref><ref name="l130">{{cite web | last=Aguilar | first=Jorge A. | title=Calibre has finally given into the AI trend | website=How-To Geek | date=2025-12-05 | url=https://www.howtogeek.com/calibre-has-finally-given-into-the-ai-trend/ | access-date=2026-02-14}}</ref>

==Features==
Calibre supports many [[file format]]s and reading devices. Most e-book formats can be edited, for example, by changing the font, font size, margins, and [[metadata]], and by adding an auto-generated table of contents. Appropriately licensed digital books can be directly converted and edited, but commercially purchased e-books may need to have [[digital rights management]] (DRM) restrictions removed first. Calibre does not natively support DRM removal, but may enable DRM removal after installing [[Plug-in (computing)|plug-ins]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Sorrel |first=Charlie |title=How To Strip DRM from Kindle E-Books and Others |url=https://www.wired.com/gadgetlab/2011/01/how-to-strip-drm-from-kindle-e-books-and-others/ |access-date=4 August 2012 |newspaper=[[Wired.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Zukerman |first=Erez |date=28 December 2012 |title=How To Break The DRM On Kindle eBooks So You Can Enjoy Them Anywhere |url=https://www.makeuseof.com/tag/how-to-break-the-drm-on-kindle-ebooks-so-you-can-enjoy-them-anywhere/ |work=MakeUseOf}}</ref>

Calibre enables users to sort and group e-books by metadata fields. Metadata can be pulled from many different sources, e.g. ISBNdb.com; online booksellers; and providers of free e-books and periodicals, such as the [[Internet Archive]], ''[[Munsey's Magazine]]'', and [[Project Gutenberg]]; and [[Social networking service|social networking]] sites for readers, such as [[Goodreads]] and [[LibraryThing]]. It is possible to search the Calibre library by various fields, such as author, title, or keyword. Full text search is available from Calibre 6.0 onwards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=calibre – New in calibre 6.0 |url=https://calibre-ebook.com/new-in/fifteen |access-date=6 May 2023 |website=calibre-ebook.com}}</ref>

E-books can be imported into the Calibre library, either by [[sideloading]] files manually or by wirelessly syncing an e-book reading device with the [[cloud storage]] service in which the Calibre library is backed up, or with the computer on which Calibre resides. Also, online content can be harvested and converted to e-books. This conversion is facilitated by so-called ''recipes'', short programs written in a [[Python (programming language)|Python]]-based [[domain-specific language]]. E-books can then be exported to all supported reading devices via [[USB]], Calibre's integrated [[Message transfer agent|mail server]], or wirelessly. Mailing e-books enables, for example, sending personal documents to the [[Amazon Kindle]] family of e-readers and [[tablet computer]]s.<ref>{{cite web |title=Transferring Kindle Books to Calibre |url=https://www.amazon.com/forum/kindle?cdForum=Fx1D7SY3BVSESG&cdThread=Tx3LTQW7QHVGARM |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161018102615/https://www.amazon.com/forum/kindle?cdForum=Fx1D7SY3BVSESG&cdThread=Tx3LTQW7QHVGARM |archive-date=18 October 2016 |access-date=24 March 2016 |website=Amazon.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=About Calibre |url=https://www.calibre-ebook.com/about |website=Calibre-ebook.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Hoffmann |first=Eric |title=EBook Software: Calibre |url=https://www.mobileread.com/forums/forumdisplay.php?f=166 |website=MobileRead Forums}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=5 December 2011 |title=Featured Tips n Tricks: How to Use Dropbox to store all your ebooks in the cloud |url=https://www.touchmyapps.com/2011/12/05/how-to-use-dropbox-to-store-all-your-ebooks-in-the-cloud/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200222180547/https://www.touchmyapps.com/2011/12/05/how-to-use-dropbox-to-store-all-your-ebooks-in-the-cloud/ |archive-date=22 February 2020 |access-date=22 February 2020 |website=TouchMyApps}}</ref>

This can be accomplished via a web browser, if the host computer is running and the device and host computer share the same network; in this case, pushing harvested content from content sources is supported on a regular interval (called 'subscription').{{citation needed|date=May 2014}} Also, if the Calibre library on the host computer is stored in a cloud service, such as [[Box (company)|Box.net]], [[Google Drive]], or [[Dropbox (service)|Dropbox]], then either the cloud service or a third-party app, such as Calibre Cloud or CalibreBox, can remotely access the library.<ref>{{cite news |last=Wallen |first=Jack |date=28 February 2011 |title=How to Use Calibre to Access Your eBook Collection Online |url=https://www.techrepublic.com/blog/linux-and-open-source/how-to-use-calibre-to-access-your-ebook-collection-online/ |work=TechRepublic}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Biba |first=Paul |date=18 February 2010 |title=How to Create Your Own Cloud of eBooks with Calibre, Dropbox, and Calibre OPDS |url=https://teleread.com/create-your-own-cloud-of-ebooks-with-calibre-dropbox-and-calibre-opds/ |work=TeleRead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Calibre2OPDS |url=https://wiki.mobileread.com/wiki/Calibre2opds |website=MobileRead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Slangen |first=Simon |date=5 August 2013 |title=How To Manage Your Ebook Collection For The Amazon Kindle With Calibre |url=https://www.makeuseof.com/tag/how-to-manage-your-ebook-collection-for-the-amazon-kindle-with-calibre/ |website=MakeUseOf}}</ref><ref name="Litte2011">{{cite web |last=Litte |first=Jane |date=24 July 2011 |title=Create Your Own Cloud of Ebooks with Calibre + Calibre OPDS... |url=https://dearauthor.com/ebooks/create-your-own-cloud-of-ebooks-with-calibre-calibre-opds-dropbox/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110418050151/http://dearauthor.com/ebooks/create-your-own-cloud-of-ebooks-with-calibre-calibre-opds-dropbox/ |archive-date=18 April 2011 |access-date=24 July 2011 |website=Dear Author}}</ref>

Since version 1.15, released in December 2013, Calibre also contains an application to create and edit e-books directly, similar to the more full-featured editor tools of the [[Sigil (application)|Sigil]] application, but without the latter's [[WYSIWYG]] editing mode.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 December 2013 |title=Calibre 1.15 eBook Manager Now Features a Native and Complete Book Editor |url=https://news.softpedia.com/news/Calibre-1-15-eBook-Manager-Now-Features-a-Native-and-Complete-Book-Editor-408803.shtml |access-date=22 September 2023 |website=news.softpedia.com}}</ref>

==Associated apps==
[[File:Calibre sync iphone.png|thumb|Synchronizing Calibre with an [[iPhone]]]]
* ''Calibre Cloud'' (free) and ''Calibre Cloud Pro'' (paid), apps by Intrepid Logic that let one "access your Calibre e-book library from anywhere in the world. Place your calibre library in your Dropbox, Box, or Google Drive folder, and be able to view, search, and download from your library anywhere".<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Calibre Cloud |url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.intrepidlogic.calibrecloud&hl=en |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160405014804/https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.intrepidlogic.calibrecloud&hl=en |archive-date=5 April 2016 |access-date=23 October 2017 |website=Google Play |publisher=Google, Inc.}}</ref> As Jane Litte at ''Dear Author'' and John Jeremy at ''Teleread'' observe: This tool can be used to "create [one's] own Cloud of eBooks"<ref name="Litte2011"/> and thereby read and allow downloads and emails from one's Calibre library via the Calibre folder in [[Box (company)|Box.net]], [[Dropbox (service)|Dropbox]], or [[Google Drive]]. Because the Calibre-generated local wireless feed ([[Open Publication Distribution system|OPDS]]) can only be accessed on devices sharing the same network as the Calibre library, this feature of the Calibre Cloud apps is particularly useful when away from one's home network, because it allows one to download and read the contents of one's Calibre library via the Calibre folder in Box, Dropbox, or Google Drive.<ref name="John Jermey">{{cite news |last=Jermey |first=John |date=30 September 2012 |title=Calibre Tools For Your Android Device |url=http://www.teleread.com/android/calibre-tools-for-your-android-device/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130618013355/http://www.teleread.com/android/calibre-tools-for-your-android-device/ |archive-date=18 June 2013 |journal=Teleread}}</ref>
* ''Calibre Companion'' (paid), an app by MultiPie, Ltd. Was recommended by calibre's developers, "brings complete integration with calibre on your desktop, giving you total control over book management on your device."<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Calibre Companion |url=https://calibrecompanion.co |access-date=23 October 2017 |website=MultiPie |publisher=MultiPie, Ltd.}}</ref> John Jermey at ''Teleread'' notes this app can manage Calibre/device libraries as if one's mobile device were plugged into computer; however, unlike Calibre Cloud, Calibre Companion requires users to be at a computer and use the Calibre-generated local wireless feed ([[Open Publication Distribution system|OPDS]]).<ref name="John Jermey" />
* ''Calibre Library'' (paid), an app by Tony Maro that allows one to "Connect wirelessly to your Calibre e-book library or other Stanza source. Browse and download your e-books on the go."<ref>{{cite news |last=Maro |first=Tony |title=Calibre Library description |url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tonymaro.calibreLibrary.apk&hl=en |access-date=23 October 2017 |journal=Google Play}}</ref> This app's operations and benefits are similar to those offered by Calibre Cloud.<ref name="John Jermey" />
* ''Calibre Sync'' (free), an app by Seng Jea Lee that "seamlessly connects to your Calibre Library and shows up as a connected device on Calibre. If Auto-Connect option is enabled, your device will attempt to connect to the Calibre Library when it is within the home Wi-Fi network. This allows Calibre to automatically update your device with the latest newspaper or magazines you have scheduled for download!"<ref>{{cite news |last=Seng |first=Jea Lee |title=Calibre Sync |url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.sengjea.calibre&hl=en |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160411035250/https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.sengjea.calibre&hl=en |archive-date=11 April 2016 |access-date=23 October 2017 |journal=Google Play}}</ref> As with Calibre Companion, this app requires the device to be on the same network as the Calibre library.
* ''CalibreBox'' (free and paid), an app by Eric Hoffmann that, like Calibre Cloud, accesses Calibre libraries from cloud storage.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hoffmann |first=Eric |title=CalibreBox |url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.hoffmann.eric.calibrebox |access-date=23 October 2017 |journal=Google Play}}</ref> Unlike Calibre Cloud, it is limited to Dropbox, but CalibreBox supports more than one library at a time, and flexible sorting and filtering. Custom column support for the book detail view, sorting, and filtering by custom columns, and adding more than two libraries are restricted to paid users. The app is built on the design principles of Google's [[Material Design]] and is under active development.<ref>{{cite news |title=CalibreBox – New Cloud-Based App |url=https://www.mobileread.com/forums/showthread.php?p=3112251 |access-date=23 October 2017 |journal=MobileRead Forums}}</ref>
* ''Calibre-go'' (free), app by Litlcode Studios lets you access your Calibre e-book library from cloud storage and access the library through Calibre-go to browse, sort, search and read books on your mobile. Calibre-go supports multiple libraries across multiple accounts simultaneously.
*Calibre Sync (paid), an Android app by BIL Studio that lets you access Calibre libraries from cloud storage ([[Dropbox (service)|Dropbox]], [[Microsoft OneDrive|OneDrive]], [[Box (company)|Box]], and Cloud), or from SD card. Calibre Sync supports multiple libraries across multiple accounts simultaneously, also allows users to browse, sort, search, filter and download books to read on devices.
